### We tell you about a price increase before it takes effect

You say to your agent

> “Is the price of an H100 going to change soon?”

A price increase now always comes at least 24 hours before it takes effect, and we tell you about it. An increase is a higher list price, or a smaller Friday, weekend, or batch job discount.

When we schedule an increase, the dashboard shows a notice until a few days after it takes effect. The admins and billing members of each organization that used that type in the last 90 days get an email.

Your agent sees it too. Until the increase takes effect, `create_node` and `get_node` carry it in `rate.upcoming_increase`, and `submit_job` carries it in `upcoming_increase`. ## October 8, 2026

1. 07:00 UTC

### The H100 price is now $5.04 per GPU-hour

On October 8 at 00:00 Pacific time, the H100 list price changed from $3.96 to $5.04 per GPU-hour. Per GPU-minute, the price changed from $0.066 to $0.084. A whole 8-GPU node now costs $40.32 per hour.

The new price applies to each minute that we bill from that time. This includes the minutes of nodes and jobs that were already running. Minutes before that time bill at the old price.

The discounts did not change, and they now apply to the new list price. Friday hours are 33% off, and Saturday and Sunday hours are 20% off, on the Pacific calendar. Batch jobs are 25% off the list price. The docs show the rates.

We did not tell you about this change before it took effect. We are sorry for the late notice. If you have a question about your bill, send it to us on the contact page.

highlights:
A canonical-data September 2026 report on H100 cloud pricing, CT-H100 constituents, freshness, and sample-composition limits.

This September report is generated from the canonical approved-provider snapshot published Sep 30, 2026. It is a dated market indicator, not a quote or a representation of today’s provider rows.

One reviewed public H100 price was selected deterministically per provider at the snapshot date

## September H100 pricing read

The September snapshot records a $4.12 CT- H100 median from 8 providers. The published median is -21.07% versus the final August history point.

- Median of one deterministically selected, current, reviewed public on-demand H100 price per provider. Quote-only, unavailable, unapproved, superseded, and expired rows are excluded.
- The headline comparison can reflect both price changes and sample composition, so it is not a pure same-provider market move.
- The six providers shared with August have an unchanged matched-provider median (0.00%). Cyfuture AI and Daytona joined the September sample; the lower headline median reflects composition rather than a uniform price cut.
- The matched-provider median uses 6 providers preserved in both dated reports; it separates repricing from changes in the headline sample.

results.title: GPU pricing is increasing across the board, but the severity of those increases varies greatly across providers.
highlights:
# GPU pricing is increasing across the board, but the severity of those increases varies greatly across providers. · 2026-09-22T00:00:00+00:00

GPU pricing is increasing across the board, but the severity of those increases varies greatly across providers.

Take H100 pricing as an example.

In 2026, providers in our network have raised their H100 rates by an average of 31.6%.

However, between these providers, their individual H100 pricing has increased as much as 47.5%, and as little as 13.6%.

Movement in GPU pricing as a whole only tells part of the story.

There is still significant price variance between operators, even those with near identical architectures.

results.title: H100 Rental Prices Jump 22% in a Month as GPU Shortage Hits Firms and Labs - Seoul Economic Daily
results.author: An Hye-ji, Intern Reporter
highlights: - Key summary: Vessl AI, a domestic neocloud company, raised the hourly rate for Nvidia H100 chips on its VESSL Cloud service to $2.98 from $2.39 on the 1st of this month, a 24.7% increase. The price adjustment marks the start of similar moves in Korea after U.S. neocloud firms including CoreWeave and Nebius successively raised GPU rental rates. Vessl AI procures most of its roughly 7,000 GPUs through leasing. According to Ornn, an AI computing trading platform, the hourly cloud rental rate for the H100 rose 21.9% over the past month to $3.28 from $2.69, reaching about 70% of the price of the higher-end H200. The impact is spreading to industry and research, with some companies abandoning bids for government-led AI transformation projects because they could not secure GPUs, while universities and research institutes scale back the size of their research.

results.title: Rental Rates for Older AI Chips Jump 25% as Demand Surges - Seoul Economic Daily
results.author: Seo Ji-hye, Kim Ji-young
highlights:
Vessl AI raised its hourly rate for Nvidia H100 graphics processing units by 24.7% starting this month, following a string of price increases by U.S. neocloud providers such as CoreWeave and Nebius amid a surge in demand for artificial intelligence computing. Supply has tightened not only for the newest chips but also for older models as demand for high-performance GPUs jumps. Other Korean cloud providers also expect to raise GPU rates depending on supply conditions, raising concerns that higher costs of securing GPUs will weigh on service development at Korean AI companies and on government AI transformation, or AX, projects.

Vessl AI on the 1st raised the hourly rate for H100 chips on its VESSL Cloud service to $2.98 from $2.39, according to AI industry sources on the 21st. The neocloud company counts leading Korean AI firms including Upstage and Motif Technologies among its clients and currently operates several thousand GPUs. It has secured about 7,000 GPUs, most of them leased rather than purchased outright. "It is hard to secure the volume we need for H100s — effectively, the price is whatever the seller names," a Vessl AI official said. "As AI demand grows, the number of customers wanting to use GPUs keeps rising, so a price adjustment was unavoidable." The company plans to expand its GPU fleet to about 10,000 units by the end of the year, but intends to keep adjusting rates flexibly to reflect supply conditions and procurement costs.

Other Korean AI cloud companies, including Elice, have also raised prices recently. In the past, rental rates for older AI GPUs fell when new models arrived, but prices for previous-generation chips are now rising as well. Hourly cloud rental rates for the H100 climbed 21.9% over the past month to $3.28 from $2.69, according to Ornn, an AI compute trading platform. That is about 70% of the price of the higher-end H200. Analysts say demand is spilling over to relatively older GPUs because supply of the newest chips cannot keep pace with surging computing demand.

results.title: NVIDIA H100 Price in 2026: What Buying and Renting Cost - Blog | GPUPerHour
results.author: Faiz Ahmed
highlights:
A single H100 80GB PCIe card last listed at $32,411.99 at CDW as retrieved on 21 September 2026, but the listing is marked Discontinued, so that is a last-seen price and not an offer. A complete 8-GPU H100 server last listed between $234,200 and $440,619.75 depending on the build, which is $29,275 to $55,077 per GPU when you divide by eight, with the CPUs, memory and network cards included. Renting one costs $2.59 per GPU-hour on QuantaCloud, which operates this site (checked 14 Nov, 12:15 UTC) right now. Buying beats that only if the GPU stays busy most of the month, and the break-even section below turns that into one division.

...

NVIDIA does not publish list prices for its data center GPUs. CNBC reported on 19 March 2024 that what a buyer pays depends on volume and on whether they buy a complete system from NVIDIA or through Dell, HP, Supermicro and similar vendors. Every H100 "price" is therefore a reseller listing, an analyst estimate or a reported transaction.

### Reseller listings on 21 September 2026

CDW listed the PNY H100 80GB PCIe card (NVH100TCGPU-KIT) at $32,411.99 on 21 September 2026, with stock status "Discontinued". CDW listed the PNY H100 NVL 94GB card (NVH100NVLTCGPU-KIT) at $32,382.99 on the same date, also "Discontinued". Both are card-only prices, and neither can be ordered.

...

The cheapest on-demand H100 across the providers we track is $2.59 per GPU-hour on QuantaCloud, which operates this site (checked 14 Nov, 12:15 UTC). The H100 comes in SXM, PCIe and NVL variants, and they do not rent for the same price:

| Variant | VRAM | Cheapest $/GPU-hr | Provider | Providers in stock |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 PCIe | 80 GB | $2.59 | QuantaCloud | 4 |
| H100 SXM5 | 80 GB | $2.90 | Ori | 5 |
| H100 NVL | 94 GB | $3.11 | Massed Compute | 2 |

Cheapest in-stock on-demand price per GPU-hour for each H100 variant, from providers with live stock tracking. Latest stock observation: 14 Nov 2026, 12:16 UTC. QuantaCloud operates this site and is ranked by price like every other provider.

Hourly prices hide the monthly bill. This table multiplies the live price out to a day and to a 730-hour month:

| GPU | $/GPU-hr | Per day (×24) | Per month (×730) | Provider |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 | $2.59 | $62.16 | $1,891 | QuantaCloud |

Cheapest in-stock on-demand price per GPU-hour, for one GPU running the whole time. Per day = hourly price × 24 hours. Per month = hourly price × 730 hours (365 days × 24 ÷ 12), rounded to the nearest dollar. Storage, data transfer and tax are not included. Latest stock observation: 14 Nov 2026, 12:16 UTC. QuantaCloud operates this site and is ranked by price like every other provider.
